### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/hono`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/http-conformance`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/adapters/hono/README.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/README.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/index.mdx`  _(via createHonoApp (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via createHonoApp (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via CORS_CREDENTIALS (literal, a string literal in HonoServerPlugin; a string literal in createHonoApp; a string literal in resolveCorsAdmission), CORS_ORIGIN (literal, a string literal in HonoServerPlugin; a string literal in createHonoApp; a string literal in resolveCorsAdmission), OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS (literal, a string literal in HonoServerPlugin; a string literal in createHonoApp; a string literal in resolveCorsAdmission), OS_CORS_ORIGIN (literal, a string literal in HonoServerPlugin; a string literal in createHonoApp; a string literal in resolveCorsAdmission))_
- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`  _(via OS_CORS_ORIGIN (literal, a string literal in HonoServerPlugin; a string literal in createHonoApp; a string literal in resolveCorsAdmission))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via OS_CORS_ORIGIN (literal, a string literal in HonoServerPlugin; a string literal in createHonoApp; a string literal in resolveCorsAdmission))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via HonoServerPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via createHonoApp (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via HonoServerPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via HonoServerPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via createHonoApp (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via createHonoApp (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/adapters/hono/README.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/README.md`, `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fcb40ad673a08b231d34190a60d692f462c5df23` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e83c8e2e4903ddfe8860e1f92ef796c66bbae630` — the merge of head `0ffd23e64de690718b939fe22ef8898c4c13f05f` into base `fcb40ad673a08b231d34190a60d692f462c5df23`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e83c8e2e4903ddfe8860e1f92ef796c66bbae630 && git checkout e83c8e2e4903ddfe8860e1f92ef796c66bbae630
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fcb40ad673a08b231d34190a60d692f462c5df23 0ffd23e64de690718b939fe22ef8898c4c13f05f && git checkout -B drift-repro fcb40ad673a08b231d34190a60d692f462c5df23 && git merge --no-ff 0ffd23e64de690718b939fe22ef8898c4c13f05f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fcb40ad673a08b231d34190a60d692f462c5df23
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fcb40ad673a08b231d34190a60d692f462c5df23` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `df7d1e1fd43c9a6aaa98729fc30ef8bbd3f1b17d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/cors-admission.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/pattern-matcher.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/hono-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/index.ts, packages/adapters/hono/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/cors-default-admission.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/pattern-matcher.test.ts, packages/adapters/hono/src/hono-cors-admission.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.cors-origin-trust.test.ts, packages/qa/http-conformance/src/cors-doors.conformance.test.ts, packages/qa/http-conformance/vitest.config.ts, packages/qa/http-conformance/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml (the whole diff outside the prose faces; The head differs from the tree the dev tested (`fb509fc0a`) in the changeset only (+3/-3), and `bb2fde296` is the same tree with an earlier changeset text. `origin/main` (`b1676441b`) is 9 commits past the merge-base; none of them moves any of the PR's 19 paths, and GitHub reports the PR mergeable. One of those commits matters to ② and ③: `06cab4849` (`chore: version packages`, PR #24524) sets `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/hono` and `@objectstack/plugin-auth` to `18.0.0`, deletes `.changeset/pre.json` (which was `mode: exit`, tag `next`, at the merge-base) and consumes `.changeset/24738-cors-default-no-cross-origin-caller.md` into the `18.0.0` CHANGELOG entries.

### ① Derived judgments

**Disclosure (security card, ruling on #9387, comment 5323310017).**
- The PR's artifacts are its title, body, the changeset, the three doc faces, the code comments in `cors-admission.ts`, `pattern-matcher.ts`, `hono-plugin.ts`, `adapter.ts`, `adapters/hono/src/index.ts` and `auth-manager.ts`, and the five commit messages.
- They state what the ruling allows and nothing further: that each of the four locations exists (an older default at `createHonoApp`, loopback beside a list in every mode, a literal-only refusal, a whole-string test in auth's merge), where each lives (file and block), and the governing text (`docs/HARDENING.md` § CORS, the go-live checklist line, #24738's Expected). The Contract table names configurations and what a door answers; it gives no request sequence against a shipped endpoint and no description of what a foreign page could obtain.
- The "Mechanism (measured)" section describes how better-auth's matcher reads a pattern class. That is the location of the auth defect, not a path through it.
- The acceptance note on `https://*.*` names an operator-written pattern class that is not refused. The previous record on this family (`6285870503`, ③ item 7) treated the same kind of statement about `https://*` as within the ruling, and this record reads it the same way: existence and location of an operator-configured class, no exploit path.
- The four new pin files drive a probe route of their own through `app.request` and read one response header, or read `options.trustedOrigins` off a real better-auth instance. They are the fix's evidence, as the claim foresaw, not a reproduction against a deployment.
- The code comments removed from `hono-plugin.ts` and `adapters/hono/src/index.ts` carried the only sentences that described the old behaviour as a mechanism; the replacements describe the rule.
- **The PR keeps to the ruling.** This record keeps to it as well: every condition below is a configuration and a file location.

**Check-runs on the head (latest run per name, 41 names, read 2026-10-20T12:45:56Z).**
- 27 are `completed/success` and 8 are `completed/skipped` (opt-in, live-DB, Console Pin Gate, the dogfood matrix shards, Auto Label, Check PR Size).
- Of the five required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded `success`. **`Test Core` is NOT MEASURED: all six shards `(1/6)` to `(6/6)` were still `in_progress` at render time. Never a pass.**
- `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. That job runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base MERGE_BASE`, so the disposition and the level form are gate-measured on this head.
- Every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` job, `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Validate Package Dependencies` and the four PR-relation checks concluded `success`.
- The earlier head `bb2fde296`'s `TypeScript Type Check` red is a cancellation by the push of `df7d1e1fd`, not a verdict, and is not read here.
- The judgments below are on the diff. The landing's own all-green check stands apart from this verdict and waits on the six shards.

**The one rule, read.** `resolveCorsAdmission` (`cors-admission.ts:75-115`): the door's option wins, else `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` (legacy `CORS_ORIGIN`, silent) through `normalizeOriginPatterns`; `credentials` is the door's option, else `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS !== 'false'`; `developmentBoot` is the input, else `isDevelopmentBoot(undefined)`, which is `NODE_ENV === 'development'` and nothing else (`stack-auth.ts:135-137`). No list: the origin handler is `developmentBoot && isLocalhostOrigin(o) ? o : null`. A list with credentials on: `normalizeOriginPatterns(configured).find(isAllHostOriginPattern)` throws, naming the entry, both variables and the door's own option. Otherwise `createOriginMatcher(configured, { developmentBoot })`. Both doors call it with their option names only (`hono-plugin.ts` about :392, `adapters/hono/src/index.ts` about :642) and hand `admission.origin` and `admission.credentials` to `hono/cors`. The adapter's old `'*'` default, its reflect-the-origin arm and its exact-string pass-through are deleted. Nothing is copied: the rule has one body.

**The matcher, read.** `matchOriginPattern` (`pattern-matcher.ts:51-63`) no longer admits a loopback origin ahead of the pattern; it answers `'*'`, exact equality, or the escaped pattern with `*` expanded to `.*`, anchored. `createOriginMatcher` (:120-138) takes `options: OriginMatcherOptions = {}`; `admitLoopback` is true only when the normalized list is non-empty AND `options.developmentBoot ?? isDevelopmentBoot(undefined)` is true, read once at creation; a loopback origin is answered before the pattern loop only when that is true. `isAllHostOriginPattern` (:76-80) is the regular expression `^(?:[^:/]+:\/\/)?\*+(?::(?:\d+|\*))?$` on the trimmed pattern: an optional scheme, one or more `*`, an optional `:port` or `:*`. It names `*`, `**`, `https://*`, `*://*`, `http://*:*`, `https://*:8443`; it does not name `https://*.*`, `*.example.com`, `https://*.example.com`, `http://localhost:*` or any exact origin.

**The PR body's `## Contract` table, row by row, against the code.** "Admitted" is the request origin echoed in `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

1. **`createHonoApp`, no list, credentials on, not a development boot: every origin with credentials, to no cross-origin caller. RIGHT.** Before: `configuredOrigin = '*'` and `credentials` true selected the reflect arm. After: the no-list handler with `developmentBoot` false answers `null` for every origin. Pinned (adapter describe 1; conformance row 1).
2. **Same, development boot: to loopback origins only, with credentials. RIGHT.** Same handler with `developmentBoot` true; `isLocalhostOrigin` admits `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`, http or https, any port. Pinned (adapter describe 1; conformance row 2).
3. **Same two, `OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS=false` (rows 3 and 4): to no cross-origin caller, or loopback only, without credentials. RIGHT.** Before: `'*'` with credentials off went through `createOriginMatcher('*')`, which echoed every origin. After: the handler never reads `credentials`; the rows differ from 1 and 2 in the credentials header only. Not pinned in the credentials-off variant; the code path is the same expression.
4. **`createHonoApp`, a list holding `*` (option or env, alone or among others), credentials on: created and every origin admitted, to a throw. RIGHT.** Before: `'*'` alone took the reflect arm; `*` inside an array or a comma string went through `hasWildcardPattern` to the matcher, whose `'*'` arm admits all. After: `isAllHostOriginPattern('*')` is true and the rule throws before any middleware is mounted; `createHonoApp` has no try around it, so the throw reaches the host. Pinned (adapter describe 3, including `' * '` and the env spellings).
5. **Both transport doors, a pattern whose host part is the bare `*`, credentials on: booted and every host the pattern matches admitted, to `init()` throws or `createHonoApp` throws. RIGHT.** Before, at both doors, such a pattern escaped the `includes('*')` test (plugin) or the `=== '*'` test (adapter) and reached the matcher, whose expansion of `https://*` is `^https://.*$`. After, the class is refused with the entry named. Both kernels rethrow an `init()` throw unwrapped, as the previous record read (`6285870503`, row 4). Pinned (plugin describe 6, five spellings, option and env, alone and in a list; adapter describe 3; conformance row 7).
6. **Both transport doors, a list with at least one pattern, not a development boot: the list plus every loopback origin, to the list only. RIGHT.** Before, both doors reached `createOriginMatcher` for a wildcard list and `matchOriginPattern` answered loopback first. After, `admitLoopback` is false outside development. Pinned (plugin describe 5 for `production`, unset and `test`; adapter describe 2; conformance rows 3 and 5).
7. **`HonoServerPlugin`, a list of exact origins only, not a development boot: the list plus every loopback origin, to the list only. RIGHT.** The plugin always used the matcher, so the convenience applied to exact lists too. Pinned (plugin describe 5, first case).
8. **`createHonoApp`, a list of exact origins only, development boot: the list only, to the list plus loopback. RIGHT, and the gain is confined.** Before, an exact list was handed to `hono/cors` as a string or array and matched exactly. After, the matcher admits loopback beside it only while `developmentBoot` is true, and `developmentBoot` is `NODE_ENV === 'development'` read when the app is created; no other input can set it, since neither door passes the option. Pinned (adapter describe 2, both boots; conformance row 4).
9. **`AuthManager`, `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` holding `*` among other entries: `*` entered the trusted set, to dropped with the others kept. RIGHT.** `auth-manager.ts` about :3026-3032: the whole-value `!== '*'` test is gone; each trimmed entry is pushed unless `admitsEveryHost(entry)`. Pinned (auth case 1; conformance row 6).
10. **`AuthManager`, `*` with surrounding space: entered, to nothing enters. RIGHT.** Before, `' * '` failed the whole-value test and its trimmed entry `'*'` was pushed. After, the trimmed entry is dropped. Pinned (auth case 2).
11. **`AuthManager`, an all-host pattern: entered, to dropped. RIGHT.** Pinned (auth case 3: `https://*`, `*://*`, `http://*:*`, `https://*:8443`; conformance rows 7 and 9).

**One row the table omits.** `createHonoApp` with `cors.origin` given as ONE comma-separated string of exact origins (no `*` anywhere), credentials either way. Before, `hasWildcardPattern` was false and the raw string went to `hono/cors` as a single exact origin, so nothing was admitted. After, `createOriginMatcher` splits it through `normalizeOriginPatterns` and admits each listed origin. The option's own TSDoc on `main` already promised "Comma-separated string or array", so this is a documented contract now honoured, and it widens only toward what the operator listed; it is covered by the `Clause-②: yes` line. The table's heading ("every input whose answer changes") and the "Unchanged" bullet ("an exact origin ... admitted as before ... at both transport doors") are one edge short for it. Not pinned. Non-blocking; the seat may name it in ACCEPT.

**"Does any configuration that admitted an origin it should keep admitting now refuse it?" No.** Every narrowing the diff makes is one the card asked for: the adapter's no-list default, loopback beside a list outside development at both doors (and at the cloud preflight, below), and the all-host class with credentials. Read for an unintended refusal: an exact origin or a host-naming pattern is admitted as before at both doors (matcher exact arm and expansion unchanged); `'*'` and an all-host pattern with credentials off still boot and echo every origin (`createOriginMatcher` with the `'*'` arm, or the expansion); an empty list (`cors.origins: []`, or `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` of whitespace) admits nothing, loopback included, on either boot, as before, since a non-empty normalized list gates `admitLoopback` (pinned, pattern-matcher test); a `cors.origin` of `''` or an `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` set to the empty string resolves to "no list" at both doors, as before at the plugin; the legacy `CORS_ORIGIN` / `CORS_CREDENTIALS` spellings are still read through `readEnvWithDeprecation`. A deployment that reached a listed-origin server from a loopback origin outside development loses that admission; that is the card's Expected and the changeset's operator step names it.

**The "Unchanged" list.** Each bullet is TRUE against the code: host-naming patterns and exact origins unchanged at both doors and in auth; the plugin's development-boot loopback beside a list and its no-list answer as #24738 left them; all-host entries with credentials off still served; the empty list; `cors: false`, `cors.enabled: false` and `OS_CORS_ENABLED=false` (both doors' guards untouched); allowed and exposed headers, methods and max-age untouched; preflights still answered by `hono/cors` whether or not an allow-origin is set; same-origin outside CORS; `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` admits nothing to CORS, since the rule reads `OS_CORS_ORIGIN` and the door's option only (ruling A, `6288093770`, holds; `serve.ts` is untouched and `OS_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` still reaches `AuthPlugin` alone).

**The two copies of the all-host predicate.** `ALL_HOST_PATTERN` in `pattern-matcher.ts:76` and the inline `admitsEveryHost` in `auth-manager.ts` about :3028 are the same regular expression character for character, and both are applied to a trimmed entry (`pattern.trim()` on the plugin side; a `.trim()` in the split's map on auth's). Equal today. **Does the enumeration pin fail if they drift?** Only on the spellings it uses: `cors-doors.conformance.test.ts` holds `ADMITS_EVERY_HOST = ['*', 'https://*']` and its rows use those two. The side pins widen that: the plugin's describe 6 and `isAllHostOriginPattern`'s own test cover `http://*`, `*://*`, `http://*:*`, `https://*:8443`, `**` and `' * '`; the auth pin covers `https://*`, `*://*`, `http://*:*` and `https://*:8443`. A drift on either copy that changes the verdict for one of those spellings fails that side's own pin. A drift confined to a spelling none of the three files use (`**` on the auth side, a bare `*:8080`, `https://**`) is caught nowhere. So "the pin holds the two equal" is true on the pinned spellings, not as a textual identity. Non-blocking for this card (③ item 7); the stronger forms are a textual-equality assertion reading both sources, or one implementation.

**Public surface.** `index.ts` adds `export * from './cors-admission'`, so `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`'s root entry (its only `exports` path) gains `resolveCorsAdmission`, `CorsAdmission`, `CorsAdmissionInput` and `CorsAdmissionDoor`; `pattern-matcher.ts` adds `isAllHostOriginPattern` and `OriginMatcherOptions` and gives `createOriginMatcher` an optional second parameter. That is exactly the list the PR body and the changeset name. `hasWildcardPattern` stays exported (the adapter no longer imports it; its test still does). `@objectstack/hono`: `ObjectStackHonoCorsOptions` keeps its shape (TSDoc only); `createHonoApp` gains a throw, documented at every face. `@objectstack/plugin-auth`: behaviour only. `HonoCorsOptions` (`adapter.ts`) is TSDoc only. `pattern-matcher.ts` now imports `@objectstack/core` at module scope; `exports` publishes the root entry only, which already loaded `hono-plugin.ts` and therefore core, so no consumer gains a new load. `Type Check · workspace` and `Build Core` concluded success. Nothing is removed or renamed, and `packages/spec` is untouched. RIGHT.

**The prose faces, each against the shipped behaviour.**
- **`docs/HARDENING.md` § CORS: TRUE.** The list row ("on a development boot, loopback origins are admitted beside the list too; on any other boot, only what the list names") and the refusal row ("`*`, or a pattern whose host part is the bare `*` ... refused at boot ... naming the entry and the two remedies") match the rule. The `createHonoApp` paragraph ("answers by the same rule, the table above holds for it too, with its own `cors.origin` option") is what the shared call makes true. The closing paragraph ("both doors refuse ... `HonoServerPlugin` at boot, `createHonoApp` when the app is created ... accepted only with credentials off ... auth never trusts it from `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`") matches the throw sites and the auth filter. The one unchanged edge from the previous record stands: an empty list admits no loopback on a development boot, narrower than the list row reads, and not a change of this diff.
- **`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/README.md`: TRUE.** Loopback "beside a list or without one" on a development boot; the refusal names the class; "exported as `resolveCorsAdmission`, and `createHonoApp` reads it too"; `createOriginMatcher(patterns, { developmentBoot })` "reads the development boot from `NODE_ENV` when the option is not passed".
- **`packages/adapters/hono/README.md`: TRUE.** The new CORS paragraph states the rule, the development-only loopback and the creation-time refusal. The options table's `cors.origin` default ("env `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`, else no list") and `cors.credentials` default ("`OS_CORS_CREDENTIALS !== 'false'`, on") match the code; the previous row said `false`, which was false against `main`'s code already, so this is a correction, not a change.
